metadata.target_audience: Co-parents, separated/divorced parents, and blended family caregivers (Ages 4–18)
metadata.core_objective: Maintain effective accountability systems without adult conflict, triangulation, or double standards between homes.

topics.title: Parallel Parenting vs. Co-Parenting
topics.summary: Establishing stability and predictability within your own home environment regardless of the other household's structure.
key_principles: Children do not require identical environments; they require predictability within each environment.
Neutral re-anchoring prevents child triangulation between homes.

topics.title: The Unified Core Threshold
topics.summary: Identifying non-negotiable safety, academic, and restorative standards across households.
core_areas: Restorative repair for major trust violations.

activities.title: Core Boundary Alignment Audit
activities.instructions: Differentiate between local household rules and cross-household core standards.

tasks.title: Shared Logistics Protocol
tasks.action: Establish business-like, fact-based communication routines for major discipline and restorative updates.

quiz.question: What is the most constructive response when a child states that the other parent has much looser rules?
options: A) Criticize the other parent so the child understands why their rules are bad.
B) Immediately loosen your own rules so the child doesn't favor the other parent.
C) State calmly that different households have different rules, and re-anchor to your home's expectations.
D) Call the other parent immediately to argue while the child watches.

quiz.question: What defines 'Parallel Parenting'?
options: A) Parents host daily meetings together to coordinate every meal and bedtime.
B) Parents in high-conflict situations disengage from one another while maintaining independent, consistent rules within their own respective homes.
C) Parents live in the same house but stay in different rooms.
D) Grandparents take over all disciplinary decisions.
